name: Card issuer risk and product lead
oneLine: Authorization decisions, fraud, disputes, Regulation E exposure.
goals: Approve legitimate agent purchases at the same rate as cardholder-present purchases.
See in the authorization message that an agent initiated the transaction, and which agent.
Bind each agentic token to a cardholder consent event and a set of limits the issuer can enforce.
Keep Regulation E and Regulation Z losses within model, even when the cardholder shared credentials with an agent.
Give cardholders a way to see and revoke agent permissions from the banking app.
Join network programs (Agentic Ready, Agent Pay enablement) without re-engineering the authorization host.
pains: Agent indicators arrive inconsistently, so the network is testing a probability score instead of a flag.
Under 12 CFR 1005.2(m), a transfer by an agent the consumer furnished credentials to is not unauthorized until notice, so the issuer and the cardholder argue over who takes the loss.

Visa has no agent-specific dispute condition and calls none of its agent rules a liability shift (Worldpay: none exists yet). Issuers must still pay for Agentic Transactions made under cardholder instructions, and from 2026-10-24 a provider's login ID counts among the evidence that can defeat a card-absent fraud dispute.
Open mandates and autonomous intent credentials can run for weeks, and the issuer has no hook to pause them.
AP2 v0.2 specifies no step-up (a failed check falls back through unresolved_constraint) and leaves liability to the networks; each network's passkey and token scheme differs.
Visa's and Mastercard's agentic tokens are different products on different networks.
decisions: Whether to enroll in network agent programs and which controls to require on agentic tokens.
Authorization strategy for agent-initiated transactions: approve, step up, or decline by segment.
How to treat disputes on agent purchases under Regulation E and Regulation Z.
What cardholder-facing controls to ship: per-agent limits, merchant lists, revoke.
